summary: registry-change-observer re-runs the full reachable_unlearned_report before its dedupe check, so probe successes fan out into catalog-wide DB reads. On every lifecycle execution-succeeded event for a probe template, dispatchRecommendationForProbe called pickTopTemplateForProbe, which re-ran the FULL report (it pages the whole template catalogue at 100 per page, runs an auto-promote dry run and reads the wide trace aggregate) BEFORE the 60 s per-(parent, target) dedupe check, so the report was computed even when the dispatch was then deduped, and once per probe execution with no rate bound. runTopologyChain also ran the same report twice: once in its fan-out and again as the conditional probe, with the identical input and a discarded result. Observed in one 12-minute DB burst: development-vessel ran the report 16 times in 8 minutes; 12 of the 16 timed out and fell back to since_iso list pages of 114-240 s each; the database ran at 5.6-9.7 cores with about 20 GB resident plus 26 GB swap and request p99 of 16-114 s, which starved node install gates. Fix: the rate check runs before the report, so a probe template report runs at most once per the existing 60 s window (keyed by the vessel-qualified probe template id), and the chain reuses its fan-out body as the probe output. Class detector still missing: nothing measures resolver invocations per window per caller, so a hot observer loop is found only from a DB burst.
must_fail: (a) 16 probe-success events for one probe template inside 60 s resolve reachable_unlearned_report once, not 16 times, and dispatch once; (b) 5 replays of one probe execution resolve it once; (c) one runTopologyChain with a non-zero total resolves it once, not twice. Red at the parent (16, 5, 2).
control: a first event still computes the report and dispatches its top template; an event after the 60 s window recomputes and dispatches; another vessel probe template has its own window.
